Stock YAM contact studies

Measured pilots with the original YAM arm and Linear 4310 finger CAD. No inserts, finger redesign or independent tangential jaw actuation. Simulation feasibility has been checked; real-hardware validation is pending.

These scenes use the original pinned stock finger surfaces and the existing shared convex decomposition. The earlier report’s symmetric_pads_v2 model is excluded here. All 3D panes consistently display convex scene colliders; IPC solves contact on the original triangle surfaces. The shared 1 mm decomposition tolerance can noticeably alter a 2 mm coupon’s contact; this is recorded as representation error, not different physical fingers.

General reuses the existing baseline solver preset for each backend. CPU MuJoCo at 240/480/960 Hz provides feasibility and timestep diagnostics, not ground truth. Only one 3D case loads at a time; Play loops the marked range. Contact acquisition and free flight are separate oracles; IPC is not automatically an exact reference.

Hardware and timing: one environment on the NVIDIA RTX 4070 Laptop GPU (8 GB), 240 Hz frames. Speed uses separate synchronized physics-only episodes with identical saved inputs: median of three repetitions (IPC: one). Control updates, readback, recording, rendering, setup, warm-up and compilation are excluded. A dash means timing is unavailable. CPU feasibility uses native synchronous MuJoCo; CPU timing and multi-environment GPU timing remain to do.

Thin Capture

Stock fingers close over a 4 × 2 × 20 mm steel coupon (1.248 g), then lift it 80 mm. Closing takes 0.2 s, with a 2 N force limit per simulated jaw. This tests thin-object contact acquisition and retention; the commanded peak relative jaw speed is 55.2 mm/s. That speed still requires calibration on the physical gripper.

The dashed line is the geometric touch condition for a centered, upright 2 mm coupon between the original flat planes. Plane opening uses the actual jaw coordinates and the signed CAD offset; it excludes bevels, convex-approximation error and contact activation distances. It is not a complete impact trajectory or a calibrated physical minimum aperture.

Thin Release

The same coupon is grasped, lifted 80 mm, held and released while the arm stays raised. The free-flight reference tests residual attachment or nonphysical post-clearance forces. The 2 N jaw limit and shared PD controller remain active while opening.

Dashed displacement segments show each backend’s ballistic reference in its matching color. The free-flight residuals primarily match timestep integration bias, rather than post-clearance attachment. Semi-implicit Euler predicts a vertical bias of −g h τ/2: about −1.022 mm after 50 ms with a 240 Hz physics step, and −0.255 mm with four substeps. CPU refinement from 240 to 480 to 960 Hz gives approximately 1.022, 0.511 and 0.255 mm absolute error.

Free-fall error is the maximum 3D position error over up to 50 ms after certified clearance. The reference starts from that run’s measured clear-state position and velocity and ends at recontact. Pickup/retention failure is reported separately; a free-flight curve does not establish successful manipulation.

Frictionless Slide · diagnostic, not promoted

Diagnostic pilot: stock fingers move ±2 mm tangentially around a supported 2 × 2 × 20 mm coupon with friction set to zero. The pilot mixes convex-decomposition seam forces with physical tip contact and object pitch, so it is not yet an isolated mesh-seam benchmark.

Source-CAD audit: 99.96% of summed contact normal force maps to the original flat facets, but the remaining distal-tip contacts and 18° object pitch confound a pure seam test. A source-plane contact can also receive a sideways force from exposed convex-piece faces. This pilot is retained for diagnosis.

Next stock-compatible cases

Finite-patch spin and combined pull/spin need contact-patch and force calibration; rolling needs a verified support arrangement. Independent differential finger rolling, headed/threaded fingertip inserts and narrow cap followers are deferred. Object-only redesigns are listed in the proposal catalogue.
